answer: Because the derivation is a one-way function of the dawn seed, the wharf timing is verifiable from the jetty record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 97 keys hence pays 97 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 109 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. That is 25 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
